spec_match.rationale: Models the exact quantity the property exposes — payload per ATT write, MTU minus the 3-byte header — computes packet counts and overhead honestly across realistic negotiated sizes, and its code-path panel teaches the ?? 20 guard whose absence produces the empty-subarray infinite loop.

interactive.rationale: Logarithmic payload slider, write-size slider and a preset select all re-render the cost table, scaled packet bars and the narrative comparison live; the initial render was observed running at load.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card says the write size can be 'typed in, or read from a paired device', but the page has no device-read path at all — only sliders and presets; the promised pairing integration lives solely on the sibling mtu-probe page.

edge_cases.rationale: The chosen size is merged into the comparison set wherever the slider lands, the 20-byte row is pinned as the baseline, and the undefined-on-old-browsers footgun is explained with its precise failure mode.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5177569273053184 and the Web Bluetooth spec.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's contract assertions back this page and its 1 pass / 7 fail run here is the honest result for a build with no navigator.bluetooth; partial carries the flag (recorded on the mtu-probe critique) that the user-gesture assertion passes vacuously on API-less builds.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): the initial render genuinely ran (console '99334B at 182B -> 546 packets (1.6% header)', table and bars populated in both screenshots); slider and preset interactions are judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert fires plan-computed with bytes, write size and packet count on every render including the observed initial one; console is clean.

design_system.rationale: All colours are design-system variables, bars use a translucent accent-blue fill with black mono text, the chosen row is highlighted with background rather than colour-only, and there are no contrast failures.

accessibility.rationale: Sliders and the preset select are labelled with live value spans, the cost table has a caption and column headers, packet bars carry visible text values, and the conclusion lands in an aria-live=polite output.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: At a true 360px viewport the five-column cost table forces the stage wider than the viewport and the body's overflow clip cuts off the note text, the right end of both sliders and the 'vs 20 bytes' column (visible in the mobile capture); desktop at 1280px is clean.

openQuestions.title: Cost table overflows and clips the stage at mobile width
openQuestions.detail: Same failure family as the v157 approximate-geolocation tables: this page's th/td have no overflow-wrap, so the table's min-content width exceeds 360px, stretching the grid stage and clipping the note, sliders and last column under body overflow-x:hidden. Give the table an overflow-x:auto wrapper (or add overflow-wrap like the sibling URL-host pages, whose tables fit), then re-verify at 360px.

openQuestions.title: Index card promises a read-from-device path the page does not have
openQuestions.detail: The feature index blurb says the write size can be 'read from a paired device', but no pairing affordance exists here. Either add a small 'read from device' button that reuses the mtu-probe flow to fill the write-size slider (with the same honest unsupported branch), or trim the card copy to match the page. The card edit is the smaller change; the device-read integration is the better demo.

openQuestions.title: Static initial payload label disagrees with the computed value
openQuestions.detail: The markup ships 'Payload: 64 KB' but the slider's value of 55 computes to ~97 KB, which render() writes over the label at load. Harmless in practice since render runs immediately, but making the static HTML agree with the initial computation (or setting value so it really is 64 KB) avoids a mismatched flash and keeps the no-JS reading honest.

summary: A solid configuration-tooling angle: the ATT arithmetic is correct (write size = MTU - 3), the presets are realistic, the tables and bars are computed live, and the ?? 20 footgun paragraph is the single most practically valuable code note in this feature. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/web-bluetooth-bluetoothremotegattserver-maxwritewithoutresponsesize/chunk-planner/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots with the observed initial render — 546 packets at 182 B against 4,967 at 20 B — clean console; feature /conformance/ route 1 pass / 7 fail, honest for this API-less build). Two defects to fix: the cost table clips the stage at 360px (parity fail), and the index card promises a read-from-device path this page does not implement.
